new_statements.quote: IV. STRESS Stress is not an important feature of Banjari. It occurs in a Banjari sentence but does not affect or alter the order of words. It is not possessed of any phonemic significance.

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no statement held by the project; every source read so far — Trail 1970, Boopathy 1974, Grierson 1907, Shantha Naik 2023 — was silent on stress). First explicit statement for the language: stress non-phonemic, sentence-level only; it gives no word-level placement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only stress statement in the thesis: stress is non-phonemic in Bastar Banjari and is treated as a sentence-level phenomenon; the suprasegmental phonemes set up (1.9.6.2, pp. 44-46) are nasalization, juncture /+/ and three terminal contours, with no word-stress phoneme and no rule for where stress falls in the word. (Verified against the page image; the scanned text layer garbles the passage.)
new_statements.exceptions: none; the lexicon (Part four) labels a few items 'stressed form of' / 'unstressed form of' (e.g. ti:n 'stressed form of tin three', tu: 'stressed form of tu you') and lists two 'stress particle' entries (to, hi), i.e. emphatic variants, not word-stress placement
new_statements.identity_note: Singh 1976 describes the Banjari of Bastar district (Jagdalpur, Kondagaon, Bijapur and Konta tahsils; then Madhya Pradesh, now Chhattisgarh), an eastern outlier of Lambadi/Banjari; Tabassum 2019 describes Lambani of north-east Karnataka (informants from Gulbarga/Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur and Bidar districts), i.e. the same region as Trail 1970 (Gulbarga). Both fall under glottocode lamb1269.

sources.citation: Trail, Ronald L. 1970. The Grammar of Lamani. SIL Publications in Linguistics and Related Fields 24. Norman: SIL/University of Oklahoma. 233 pp. (PhD, Univ. of Poona 1968).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology ch. 1 (pp. 7-26): consonants, vowels, nasalization as the sole suprasegmental phoneme (1.1.3 p. 7; 1.2.3 p. 15), syllable ±C±C+V±C±C (1.3.1 p. 16), clusters, open transition, morphophonemics. No stress/accent statement; no stress symbol in the Apparatus (p. 224). Obtained via the Internet Archive (2023-12-08 capture) of the sil.org reapdata PDF, sil.org itself being could not be reached by automated download.
